capability: Distribution-free calibrated prediction intervals plus quantitative applicability-domain attestation for epoxy-amine coating glass transition temperature (Tg, K) on the Polyuniverse Epoxy 1M dataset (N=96,504 scaffold-safe sampled polymers, 1,842 unique Bemis-Murcko amine scaffolds). Implements the split-conformal algorithm (Papadopoulos-Proedrou-Vovk-Gammerman 2002) with GroupKFold scaffold-safe train/cal/test partition, Morgan-fingerprint Tanimoto applicability-domain scoring (OECD 2007 QSAR Guidance Principle 3; Roy-Kar-Ambure 2015), coverage stratified by AD quintile, and hostile-null shuffle falsifiability test. Grants no scoring, batch-release, manufacturing-qualification, or optimizer authority.

fitted_or_physical_model_artifact.applicability_domain_rule: AD_score(x_new) = max over training scaffolds s of TanimotoSimilarity(Morgan(x_new), Morgan(s)). Low AD score flags out-of-distribution chemistry where model reliability is expected to degrade.
fitted_or_physical_model_artifact.conformal_prediction_rule: interval = [ŷ - q̂_α, ŷ + q̂_α] where q̂_α is the ⌈(1-α)(n_cal+1)⌉-th order statistic of |y_i - ŷ(x_i)| on the scaffold-disjoint calibration set. Marginal coverage ≥ 1-α by Papadopoulos et al 2002 under exchangeability.
fitted_or_physical_model_artifact.feature_matrix: amine Morgan(r=2, 256 bits) ⊕ epoxy Morgan(r=2, 256 bits) ⊕ 9 numeric MD-descriptors

metrics.name: marginal_conformal_coverage_at_alpha_010_meets_target
metrics.note: Fraction of 10,279 scaffold-safe held-out epoxy-amine polymer Tg observations whose values fall inside the split-conformal prediction interval at nominal miscoverage α=0.10. Coverage guarantee ≥ 1 - α = 0.90 by Papadopoulos, Proedrou, Vovk, Gammerman 2002 under exchangeability of calibration and test sets, which is preserved here because both sets are drawn from held-out scaffolds via the same random permutation.

metrics.name: marginal_conformal_coverage_at_alpha_020_meets_target
metrics.note: Same guarantee at α=0.20 (target 0.80). Second alpha level to verify the guarantee is not an artifact of α=0.10.

metrics.name: hostile_null_shuffle_coverage_at_alpha_010_meets_target
metrics.note: y values shuffled once with np.random.default_rng(seed=0); features and scaffold-safe train/cal/test splits preserved; split-conformal recomputed. Coverage guarantee derives from exchangeability only and should be preserved when y is exchangeably shuffled. This is a direct empirical falsification test of the coverage claim.

metrics.name: hostile_null_width_inflates_over_real_signal
metrics.note: Ratio of hostile-null median interval width to real-signal median interval width, both at α=0.10. Under a shuffled y the base learner cannot fit any real signal so calibration residuals must inflate, widening the conformal intervals. A ratio > 1 is direct quantitative evidence the base learner has extracted real signal beyond the exchangeability coverage guarantee alone.

metrics.name: worst_ad_quintile_coverage_at_alpha_010_meets_worst_case_floor
metrics.note: Worst (minimum) coverage across five applicability-domain quintiles at α=0.10. AD score is Morgan fingerprint Tanimoto to the nearest training scaffold representative (Bemis-Murcko amine scaffold). Per-quintile (conditional) coverage is NOT theoretically guaranteed by split-conformal — a low value flags a distribution-shift regime. Reporting the worst quintile is an early-warning indicator. Soft floor 1-2α = 0.80 is a permissive threshold; a violation would prompt AD-restricted use only.

metrics.name: worst_ad_quintile_coverage_at_alpha_020_meets_worst_case_floor
metrics.note: Second AD-conditional coverage check at α=0.20 (soft floor 0.60).

metrics.name: test_r2_positive_scaffold_safe
metrics.note: Test-set coefficient of determination on the 10,279 scaffold-safe held-out epoxy-amine polymers. Positive means the base learner outperforms a mean baseline on genuinely novel amine scaffolds. Combined with the coverage guarantee this establishes that the conformal intervals wrap a real signal.

metrics.name: byte_stable_two_replay_pipeline
metrics.note: Observational. Full pipeline (100k-polymer load, Morgan FP + descriptor featurization, scaffold-safe split, 3 HistGradientBoostingRegressor fits, split-conformal calibration, AD Tanimoto over ~5M pairs, hostile-null replay) is deterministic under seed=0 and produces byte-identical signed receipts across two consecutive runs.

population: Polyuniverse Epoxy 1M: 1,000,000 di-amine × di-epoxide computed polymer structures with MD-simulated Tg (K). N=96,504 sampled with rng seed 0 (bit-exactly matches parent Polyuniverse-Epoxy Tg/YM receipt). 1,842 distinct Bemis-Murcko generic amine scaffolds; scaffold-safe partition into train=1,106, cal=368, test=368 scaffolds. y_stats: mean 119.5 K, std 25.5 K, range [14.1, 247.9] K. Hostile-null: same features and scaffold splits, y shuffled once with np.random.default_rng(0).
split_methodology: 60/20/20 scaffold-safe train / calibration / test partition by unique Bemis-Murcko amine scaffold. Random permutation of unique scaffolds under np.random.default_rng(seed=0); first 20% → test, next 20% → calibration, remaining 60% → train. Assertion of pairwise scaffold-disjointness at construction time. Conformal calibration on scaffold-disjoint held-out polymers, empirical coverage measurement on further scaffold-disjoint held-out polymers. Applicability domain scoring uses each test polymer's amine-scaffold Morgan fingerprint Tanimoto similarity to the closest training-scaffold representative.
